literal: Changsun Song; Changsun Daosheng
idiomatic: Biographies of Changsun Song and Changsun Daosheng

literal: Changsun Song was a man of Dai; the Founding Emperor bestowed the name on him.
idiomatic: Changsun Song came from Dai; Taizu gave him the name by which he is known.

literal: His father Ren, in Emperor Zhaocheng's reign, was southern grandee.
idiomatic: His father Ren had served as southern grandee under Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: Song was magnanimous and refined and possessed of bearing; at fourteen he took his father's place in command of the army.
idiomatic: Broad-minded, graceful, and statesmanlike, Song at fourteen succeeded his father in command of the host.

literal: In the closing years of Zhaocheng the tribes fell into disorder; Fu Jian had Liu Kuren oversee state affairs; Song with Yuan Ta and others led their followers to submit to him.
idiomatic: When Zhaocheng's reign was ending the tribes turned unruly; Fu Jian set Liu Kuren to govern the realm, and Song with Yuan Ta and the rest brought their people in to him.

literal: When Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Song led more than seven hundred households of old followers and native places in deserting Xian and fleeing, [2] intending to reach Wuyuan.
idiomatic: At Liu Xian's treason Song broke away with seven hundred-odd households of old retainers and home districts, [2] making for Wuyuan.

literal: At that time Shijun's son also gathered forces and set himself up; Song wished to join him.
idiomatic: Shijun's son had meanwhile mustered men and declared himself leader; Song meant to go over to him.

literal: Meeting at Wuwo, he called himself the son of a rebellious father and urged Song to submit to Taizu.
idiomatic: At Wuwo he met Song, styled himself a son who had turned against his father, and pressed him to submit to Taizu.

literal: Song was undecided; Wuwo turned his ox's head about, and Song bowed low and followed.
idiomatic: Song still hesitated until Wuwo swung his ox about on the road; then Song bowed his head and went along.

literal: He met Taizu at Sanhan Pavilion.
idiomatic: He presented himself to Taizu at Sanhan Pavilion.

literal: When Taizu assumed the great succession, he again made him southern grandee.
idiomatic: Once Taizu took the great mandate, he restored Song as southern grandee.

literal: He repeatedly distinguished himself in military merit.
idiomatic: Battle after battle he piled up honors on the field.

literal: Later he followed the campaign against Zhongshan, was made inspector of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: He later marched against Zhongshan, was named inspector of Jizhou, and enfeoffed Duke of Julu.

literal: He served in succession as attendant-in-ordinary, minister over the masses, and inspector of Xiangzhou; was enfeoffed Duke of Nanping and won renown wherever he was posted.
idiomatic: He rose through attendant-in-ordinary, minister over the masses, and inspector of Xiangzhou, was made Duke of Nanping, and wherever he served his name was praised.

literal: When Taizong took the throne, he with Marquis of Shanyang Xi Jin, Marquis of Beixin An Tong, Marquis of Baima Cui Hong, and five others — eight in all — sat to the right of the Halting-Chariot Gate hearing and deciding the myriad affairs of state; hence the age called them the Eight Lords.
idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he joined Xi Jin, Marquis of Shanyang, An Tong, Marquis of Beixin, Cui Hong, Marquis of Baima, and five others — eight men who sat to the right of the Halting-Chariot Gate to hear and settle the realm's business — and men of the time called them the Eight Lords.

literal: When the Jin general Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong, Taizong lent Song his tally of authority and made him overseer of all military affairs east of the mountains; he was sent to Pingyuan, marched along the north bank of the Yellow River, and drew up his army at Pancheng.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu of Jin marched against Yao Hong, Taizong lent Song his staff and made him overseer of armies east of the mountains; he went to Pingyuan, followed the north bank of the Yellow River, and encamped at Pancheng.

literal: The army met with considerable setbacks.
idiomatic: The campaign went badly in several clashes.

literal: An edict granted Liu Yu passage; from his boat Yu gazed at Song's banners and canopies and sent him wine from Ling and foods of the Jiang region; Song had them all forwarded to the capital.
idiomatic: An edict granted Liu Yu free passage; from his boat Yu looked on Song's banners and sent Ling wine and delicacies of the south — Song forwarded everything to the capital.

literal: An edict ordered Song to reply with generous gifts.
idiomatic: The court ordered Song to return the courtesy in full measure.

literal: He further charged him to select elite troops for war readiness: if Yu passed westward, Song was to lead picked forces south into Peng and Pei; if Yu did not pass in season, he was only to trail the army with his own.
idiomatic: He also told him to pick crack troops for battle: if Yu crossed west, strike south into Peng and Pei with the elite; if Yu did not pass on schedule, simply follow with the host.

literal: When they reached the Xiao-Shan corridor they would surely grapple with Yao Hong — one side dead, one wounded, their strength spent.
idiomatic: By the time they reached the country between Xiao and Shan they would be locked with Yao Hong — one dead, one hurt, both armies spent.

literal: Wait until autumn moon, then strike at leisure, and Liu Yu's head might hang without a battle.
idiomatic: Wait until the autumn moon, move at ease, and Liu Yu's head might be taken without a fight.

literal: Thereupon Shusun Jian and others followed the river toward Luoyang.
idiomatic: Shusun Jian and the rest then followed the river toward Luoyang.

literal: They then entered the passes.
idiomatic: They entered the passes.

literal: [3] Song with Jian and the rest crossed south from Chenggao; every Jin garrison they met fled at the dust of their approach.
idiomatic: [3] Song and Jian crossed south from Chenggao; Jin outposts everywhere broke and ran at their dust.

literal: When Yu took Chang'an, Song withdrew his army.
idiomatic: Once Liu Yu had Chang'an, Song led the army home.

literal: Taizong lay ill in bed and asked Song about the succession; Song said: "To establish the eldest is accordance with order; to establish by virtue is to win men's hearts.
idiomatic: Taizong, bedridden, asked Song about the succession; Song said: "To set up the eldest is to follow order; to set up by virtue is to win hearts.

literal: The eldest imperial son is worthy and the hereditary heir — Heaven's mandate; I beg that he be established.
idiomatic: The eldest imperial son is able and the rightful heir — Heaven has chosen him; I beg that he be established.

literal: " Thus the decision was fixed within the palace precincts.
idiomatic: " With that the choice was settled inside the palace.

literal: Thereupon an edict had Shizu attend court and oversee the state; Song was made left supporter.
idiomatic: An edict then had Shizu preside at court and oversee the realm; Song was made left supporter.

literal: When Shizu took the throne, Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping and made rectifier of Sima province.
idiomatic: At Shizu's accession Song was raised to Prince of Beiping and made rectifier of Sima province.

literal: An edict asked the ministers whether to campaign first against the Helian or the Rouran.
idiomatic: The Emperor asked the ministers whether the Helian or the Rouran should be attacked first.

literal: Song with Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han, Minister of Works Xi Jin, and others said: "The Helian hold to their soil and cannot yet be a grave threat; the Rouran have for generations been a frontier scourge — it is right to strike Dadan first.
idiomatic: Song with Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, Xi Jin, Minister of Works, and the rest said: "The Helian cling to their land and are not yet a great peril; the Rouran have long harried the border — strike Dadan first.

literal: If we reach them in time and seize their herds, that alone will enrich the state;
idiomatic: Catch them in time and take their livestock and the realm grows rich;

literal: if we do not reach them, hunt the Yin Mountains, slaughter beasts in number, and fill the army's stores with hide, flesh, sinew, and horn — that too is better than crushing a petty state.
idiomatic: if not, hunt the Yin Mountains, kill game in masses, and stock the host with hide, meat, sinew, and horn — still better than breaking some small kingdom.

literal: " Grand Minister of Ceremonials Cui Hao said: "Dadan shifts like birds in flight; a swift pursuit cannot be sustained, and a great host cannot overtake him.
idiomatic: " Cui Hao, Grand Minister of Ceremonials, said: "Dadan vanishes like migrating birds — hot pursuit cannot last, and a great army cannot catch him.

literal: Helian Qugai's domain is no more than a thousand li; his punishments and government are cruel — abandoned by men and spirits alike; he should be attacked first.
idiomatic: Helian Qugai holds barely a thousand li; his laws are savage and men and gods alike have turned from him — attack him first.

literal: " Minister of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie and Marquis of Wujing An Yuan asked to pacify Feng Bo first.
idiomatic: " Liu Jie of the Masters of Writing and An Yuan, Marquis of Wujing, urged that Feng Bo be subdued first.

literal: [4] The Emperor was silent and thereafter went west on tour.
idiomatic: [4] The Emperor said nothing and went west on a hunting tour.

literal: Later, hearing that Qugai had died and that Guanzhong was in great disorder, the court debated an expedition.
idiomatic: Later word came that Qugai was dead and Guanzhong in turmoil; the court debated marching west.

literal: Song and the others said: "If they hold the walls and meet our strength with ease, Dadan will hear of it and raid while we are exposed — a perilous road.
idiomatic: Song and the rest said: "If they sit behind walls and trade our strength for their rest, Dadan will hear and strike our flank — a dangerous course.

literal: " The Emperor then asked the subtle signs of Heaven from the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi; [5] Qianzhi urged the march.
idiomatic: " The Emperor then asked the Celestial Master Kou Qianzhi for Heaven's hidden signs; [5] Qianzhi urged him to go.

literal: Du Chao endorsed it; [6] Cui Hao again spoke of the profit in a western campaign.
idiomatic: Du Chao backed the plan; [6] Cui Hao again argued the gain of a western war.

literal: Song and the others firmly remonstrated that it could not be done.
idiomatic: Song and his party remonstrated hard that the move must not be made.

literal: The Emperor was furious, accused Song of corruption in office, and had armored men publicly humiliate him.
idiomatic: The Emperor flew into rage, charged Song with graft in office, and had warriors shame him in public.

literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Before long he was moved to Grand Commandant.

literal: After a long while he was given the added title Grand General with Pillar of State.
idiomatic: Years later he received the added rank Grand General with Pillar of State.

literal: From then on, whenever the imperial carriage went on campaign, Song as an elder statesman mostly remained to guard the capital, sitting in the hall of court and judging criminal cases.
idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the Emperor marched out, Song — by then the senior man of the court — usually stayed to hold the capital, presiding in the hall of court to settle suits at law.

literal: He died at eighty.
idiomatic: He passed away at eighty.

literal: Posthumous title: King Xuan.
idiomatic: He was posthumously titled King Xuan.

literal: Later Emperor Gaozu, recalling the merit of the former court, had Song enshrined to share sacrifice in the temple hall.
idiomatic: Later Gaozu, honoring the founders, had Song given a place in the ancestral temple.

literal: His son Tui was skilled at mounted archery and could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
idiomatic: His son Tui excelled in horsemanship and archery and bent a three-hundred-jin bow.

literal: He inherited the rank and was made attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Campaigns South.
idiomatic: He inherited the title, was made attendant-in-ordinary, and named General Who Campaigns South.

literal: For an offense he was reduced to garrison soldier; later his noble rank was restored.
idiomatic: Convicted of a crime, he was demoted to frontier garrison duty; his noble rank was later restored.

literal: He died; posthumous title King An.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled King An.

literal: His son Dun, styled Xiaoyou, held the post of chief general of the northern garrison.
idiomatic: His son Dun, whose style was Xiaoyou, served as chief general of the northern garrison.

literal: For venality he was demoted to duke.
idiomatic: Graft in office cost him his princely rank; he was made a duke.

literal: In Emperor Gaozong's reign he himself praised the weight of his forebears' service; [7] his kingly rank was restored.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he himself recited the heavy merit of his line; [7] his royal title was restored.

literal: He died; posthumous title King Jian.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled King Jian.

literal: His son Dao, styled Nianseng, inherited the rank.
idiomatic: His son Dao, styled Nianseng, inherited the title.

literal: After a long while, by the usual rule he was demoted to duke and held the post of General of the Right Guard.
idiomatic: In time, under the usual demotion, he became a duke and served as General of the Right Guard.

literal: He died; posthumous name Shen.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Shen.

literal: His son Yue inherited the rank.
idiomatic: His son Yue inherited the title.

literal: At the opening of the Jianyi era his original kingly rank was restored; soon he was again demoted to duke.
idiomatic: At the start of Jianyi his royal title was restored; before long he was reduced again to duke.

literal: He held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Enfeoffments.
idiomatic: He served as Vice Director of the Palace Enfeoffments.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

literal: Changsun Daosheng was Song's cousin's son.
idiomatic: Changsun Daosheng was Song's nephew.

literal: Steadfast, loyal, and scrupulous, Taizu loved his careful manner and put him in charge of confidential affairs; with He Pi and three others he attended within at the left and right, bearing edicts in and out.
idiomatic: Steadfast, loyal, and careful, he won Taizu's trust for his gravity; Taizu set him over secret matters, and with He Pi and three others he waited on the throne, carrying orders in and out.

literal: When Taizong took the throne, he was made General of the Southern Command and inspector of Jizhou.
idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was named General of the Southern Command and inspector of Jizhou.

literal: Later he took a beautiful woman and presented her to Taizong; Taizong sternly rebuked him but, as an old servant, did not punish or dismiss him.
idiomatic: Later he took a beautiful woman and offered her to Taizong; Taizong rebuked him sharply yet, as a veteran of the founding, withheld punishment or dismissal.

literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Ruyin; [8] he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he was raised to Duke of Ruyin; [8] he was moved to Minister of Justice.

literal: He followed the campaign against the Rouran; with Wei Juan and others he led forces out between the White and Black Deserts and returned in great victory.
idiomatic: He marched against the Rouran; with Wei Juan and others he led troops through the country between the White and Black Deserts and came back in triumph.

literal: When Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Minister of Works Changsun Han and Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing served as vanguard and thereupon pacified the state.
idiomatic: On Shizu's campaign against Helian Chang, Daosheng with Changsun Han, Minister of Works, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led the van and brought the realm down.

literal: Chang's younger brother Ding fled to hold Pingliang; Liu Yilong sent the generals Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde to raid Henan and rescue Ding.
idiomatic: Chang's brother Ding withdrew to Pingliang; Liu Yilong sent Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde to strike Henan and relieve Ding.

literal: An edict ordered Daosheng with Prince of Danyang Taizhi to encamp on the river and resist them.
idiomatic: The court ordered Daosheng and Taizhi, Prince of Danyang, to hold the river line against them.

literal: They thereupon lured Liu Yilong's general Tan Daoji, caught him between front and rear, pursued him to Licheng, and returned.
idiomatic: They baited Tan Daoji of Liu Yilong's host, caught him fore and aft, chased him to Licheng, and withdrew.

literal: He was made Minister of Works, added attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced to Prince of Shangdang.
idiomatic: He was named Minister of Works and attendant-in-ordinary and raised to Prince of Shangdang.

literal: He died at eighty-two.
idiomatic: He passed away at eighty-two.

literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant; posthumous name Jing.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous name Jing.

literal: Daosheng was frugal; though he held one of the Three Excellencies, his clothes bore no rich ornament and his meals no second dish.
idiomatic: Daosheng lived sparely: though a pillar of state, he wore no finery and ate but one course.

literal: A single bear-pelt mud-guard he did not change for decades; men of the time compared him to Yan Ying.
idiomatic: One bear-hide riding apron he kept for decades without replacing; his contemporaries likened him to Yan Ying.

literal: His house was low and mean; after he went out on garrison duty his sons and nephews somewhat repaired it and raised halls and galleries.
idiomatic: His dwelling was humble; once he had left on frontier command his sons and nephews refurbished it and built halls.

literal: When Daosheng returned he sighed and said: "In old times Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed he would not concern himself with a household — and now strong foes still wander the soul of the northern desert; how can I sit at ease amid splendor!
idiomatic: On his return Daosheng sighed: "Huo Qubing once said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed a man had no business with a home — and mighty enemies still haunt the northern sands; how should I dwell in comfort and show?

literal: " He thereupon sternly rebuked his sons and nephews and ordered the house destroyed.
idiomatic: " He rebuked his sons and nephews harshly and made them tear the house down.

literal: Such was his respectful caution.
idiomatic: In such ways he kept his reverent care.

literal: In Shizu's age he won distinction wherever he served; whenever he framed a great proposal it mostly matched the moment.
idiomatic: Under Shizu he left his mark in every post; on great questions his counsel usually hit the hour.

literal: As a general he had stratagem and treated officers and men well.
idiomatic: In command he was resourceful and kind to his troops.

literal: The Emperor ordered singing masters to go through the ministers in praise, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, frugal as Daosheng.
idiomatic: The Emperor had singers pass among the ministers in praise, saying: "Wise as Cui Hao, spare as Daosheng.

literal: " In his old age he was much swayed by his wife Lady Meng, for which he was mocked.
idiomatic: " In age he fell under his wife Lady Meng's sway and was laughed at for it.

literal: He and his uncle Song both held one of the Three Excellencies — an honor for their generation.
idiomatic: He and his uncle Song both reached the Three Excellencies — a glory of their day.

literal: His son Kang, [9] held the post of Vice Director; he died young.
idiomatic: His son Kang, [9] served as Vice Director and died young.

literal: Kang's son Guan, in youth famed for bold courage, later inherited his grandfather's rank as Prince of Shangdang.
idiomatic: Kang's son Guan won early fame for fierce courage and later inherited his grandfather's title as Prince of Shangdang.

literal: At that time most kings of other surnames who inherited were demoted to duke; because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding court, the Emperor specially did not lower his rank.
idiomatic: By then most non-imperial clansmen who inherited were cut to duke; because Daosheng had served the founding, the Emperor left Guan's princely rank untouched.

literal: He was made General Who Campaigns West, acting Minister of Works, and overseer of the seven garrisons of the Hexi circuit, to campaign against Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: He was named General Who Campaigns West, acting Minister of Works, and overseer of the seven Hexi garrisons to strike Tuyuhun.

literal: The tribal chief Shiyin fled into hiding; Guan burned his towns and strongholds and returned.
idiomatic: The Tuyuhun chief Shiyin vanished into concealment; Guan burned his settlements and withdrew.

literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign he was made Director in the Palace Department and attendant-in-ordinary.
idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign he was made Director in the Palace Department and attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: When Tuyuhun again pressed the border, Guan was again lent the acting rank of Minister of Works to subdue them.
idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided again, Guan was again lent the acting seal of Minister of Works to bring them to heel.

literal: Later he was made General Who Campaigns South.
idiomatic: He was later named General Who Campaigns South.

literal: He died; posthumous name Ding.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Ding.

literal: His funeral followed the precedent of his grandfather King Jing and he was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.
idiomatic: His burial followed his grandfather King Jing's rites, and he was laid to rest beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.
